post_summary_truncated.description: True when the summary still hit the model's token ceiling after auto-continuation; the text was trimmed to its last complete sentence.

watchlist_alert.description: True if the post or its comments mention an 'always' stance target.

language_method.description: Which detector produced `language`. fastText is optional; without it the pipeline degrades to script detection rather than failing the post, and `language_confidence` should be read accordingly.

text_sentiment.description: Caption sentiment with its own score; null for null-caption posts.

image_sentiment.description: Aggregate image sentiment with its own score; null for text-only posts.

coverage.description: analyzed / commentCount, clamped to 1.0. When the stored rows exceed the reported count the excess is reported in coverage_anomaly, never as coverage above 100%.

coverage_anomaly.description: Set when analyzed > the platform's reported commentCount — an upstream data-quality event, not a coverage figure.

summary.description: LLM-written natural-language summary of the comment reactions.

summary_source.description: How the comment summary was produced (e.g. 'llm').

sentiment_breakdown.description: Counts over ALL comments, including emoji-only reactions.

sentiment_breakdown_substantive.description: The same counts over written comments only (emoji-only reactions excluded) — what people SAID, as opposed to how the crowd reacted.

reaction_only.description: Comments that are emoji/punctuation only. Kept as crowd signal, never sent to an LLM.

target_stances.description: Per-watchlist-entity stance rollup (stance_targets.md). A SEPARATE measurement from sentiment_breakdown — a comment can be positive in tone while opposing a listed entity, and the two must never be summed or merged. Entities nobody mentioned are ABSENT, not zero-filled: 'nobody discussed X' and 'everyone was neutral on X' are different findings. The watchlist itself is a stated bias model, not a neutral measurement.

polarity.description: As declared in the watchlist — an editorial choice by the operator.

aliases_matched.description: Which spelling matched, and how often — the fastest way to debug alias coverage.

emotion_breakdown.description: Count of comments per emotion label (full coverage).

method_breakdown.description: Count of comments per labelling method. Only the methods that actually ran appear — a zeroed 'model' bucket would imply an inference that never happened.

provenance.description: Where this post's comment labels came from, so a sentiment chart can state its own provenance alongside coverage.

inferred.description: Labels produced by a model or an LLM.

heuristic.description: Labels from the emoji/lexicon fast path or the deterministic hash stub.

method.description: How this label was produced. 'stub' is the deterministic hash fallback used in MODEL_STUB_MODE or when a model is unavailable — it is reproducible, and it is not sentiment.

kind.description: How much text the comment contains. 'emoji' comments carry no word tokens and are never sent to an LLM. 'filtered' are filtered by the router.

emotion_method.description: Emotion is the free emoji+lexicon heuristic at Stage 1 for EVERY comment, even in real mode where a transformer emotion head is loaded and used for the post. Stage 2 upgrades only the comments it re-labels. Without this field emotion_breakdown looked like model output.

target_stances.description: Stance toward each watchlist entity this comment mentions. Absent when it mentions none. Never merged into 'sentiment'.

evidence.description: The text the verdict was based on — makes a wrong call debuggable.

role_models.description: {role: resolved model id} for this run. Summarization ('summary') and classification ('stage2') can be different models, so a single llm_model cannot attribute the summary.

degraded_components.description: Real-mode components that fell back to a heuristic because their model would not load (language, sentiment, emotion, toxicity, vision, ner, keywords, embedding). nlp_engine says which path was INTENDED; this says what actually ran. A non-empty list here means the output is partly or wholly heuristic despite MODEL_STUB_MODE=false.

nlp_engine.description: Which Stage-1 engine was INTENDED. Read together with degraded_components, which says what actually ran.

stub_mode.description: MODEL_STUB_MODE. When true, sentiment labels and embeddings are deterministic hashes rather than model output — see comment_analysis.provenance and embedding_is_stub.

vision_used.description: A photo post went down the vision path.

vision_produced_signal.description: A vision model actually returned a verdict. Only this licenses a claim about image sentiment; vision_used alone does not.

model_versions.description: Concrete model ids that produced this result, for reproducibility.
